title: 모임 사회 보기: 순서가 바뀌고, 말이 길어질 때
objective: Run a meeting in Korean, change the order, politely cut someone off, and use -ㄴ/는다면 / -다면 for conditional instructions.
summary: Learn how a host keeps a meeting on track when a speaker is late or someone talks too long.
setting: A monthly meeting of a neighborhood club in a small community room. Mark is hosting for the first time. The first presenter is late, and one member talks for too long during introductions.

task.title: Run the meeting
task.line: Use the dialogue and expressions on page 1 to complete each item.

words.example: 이번 송년회는 제가 사회를 보기로 했어요.
words.exampleMeaning: I've agreed to host this year-end party.

words.meaning: to hear from someone (a call or message comes)
words.example: 아직 민수 씨한테서 연락이 안 왔어요.
words.exampleMeaning: I haven't heard from Minsu yet.

words.example: 말씀 중에 죄송한데요, 마이크가 꺼져 있어요.
words.exampleMeaning: Sorry to interrupt, but your mic is off.

words.meaning: to move on (to the next item)
words.example: 이 이야기는 여기까지 하고 다음 주제로 넘어갈까요?
words.exampleMeaning: Shall we stop this topic here and move on to the next one?

words.meaning: 'if you…' (polite). Use -(으)신다면 with action verbs and -(으)시다면 with adjectives and 있다. A host uses it to give soft instructions.
words.exampleMeaning: If you're going to leave early, please let us know now.

dialogue.korean: 원래 첫 순서는 지수 씨 발표인데, 조금 늦는다고 연락이 왔어요. 그래서 자기소개부터 하겠습니다.
dialogue.meaning: Jisu's talk was supposed to be first, but she let us know she's running a little late. So we'll start with introductions.

dialogue.korean: 괜찮으시다면 이름하고 모임에 오게 된 이유만 짧게 말씀해 주세요.
dialogue.meaning: If you don't mind, just briefly tell us your name and why you came.

dialogue.korean: 네, 저는 준호인데요. 이 모임을 처음 알게 된 건 작년 봄이었는데, 그때 회사 일이 너무 바빠서…
dialogue.meaning: Sure, I'm Junho. I first heard about this group last spring, but back then I was really busy at work, so...

dialogue.korean: 준호 씨, 말씀 중에 죄송한데요. 시간이 좀 부족해서 나머지 이야기는 쉬는 시간에 이어서 해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.meaning: Junho, sorry to interrupt. We're a bit short on time. Could you finish the rest of your story during the break?

dialogue.korean: 아니에요, 마침 잘 오셨어요. 준비되셨다면 바로 발표로 넘어가겠습니다. 다들 박수 부탁드립니다.
dialogue.meaning: That's OK, you came at just the right time. If you're ready, we'll go straight to your talk. Everyone, a round of applause, please.

exercises: Fill in the blank with the -는다면 form of 남다: 시간이 ____ 한 분만 더 말씀을 듣겠습니다.
Choose what the host should say first. A member is talking too long and time is short: ⓐ 말씀 중에 죄송한데요 ⓑ 박수 부탁드립니다 ⓒ 마침 잘 오셨어요
Make each phrase a polite condition with -(으)시다면 or -(으)신다면: ① 자리가 불편하다 → ____ 말씀해 주세요. ② 다음 모임에도 오다 → ____ 미리 연락해 주세요. ③ 사진을 원하다 → ____ 끝나고 같이 찍어요.
Answer in Korean: The first presenter is running late. Tell the group that you will change the order.
answers: ① 불편하시다면 ② 오신다면 ③ 원하신다면
(예시 답) 발표하실 분이 조금 늦으셔서 순서를 바꾸겠습니다. / 다른 답도 가능합니다. 예: 지수 씨가 조금 늦는다고 해서 순서를 바꾸겠습니다.
